newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian shares buoyed by brewery stock.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian shares buoyed by brewery stock.

text.p: Sustained demand for Nigerian Breweries dominated the stock market on Tuesday, traders said.
The all-share index gained nearly 10 points to close at 6654.54 from 6644.86 on Monday.
Nigerian Breweries rose 35 kobo, its biggest one-day gain this year, to 10.60 naira as investors resumed buying the stock that until Monday had been sliding since January.
"Nigerian Breweries is headed back up," one trader said. "Its management has made an impressive re-organisation including diversifying into the expanding soft drinks business."
But another brewer, Guinness was still not out of the woods. It fell 10 kobo on Tuesday to close at 6.80 naira.
Several blue chips again lost ground but overall gainers outweighed lossers.
Lever Brothers was down five kobo at 25.30 naira as investors continued to sell in anticipation of Christmas expenses. Cadbury fell three to 25.95 naira for the same reason.
Conglomerate UAC dropped 10 kobo to 9.25 naira on the sale of 500,000 shares.

Nestle Foods ended higher at 39.60 naira, up 40 kobo. Union Dicon Salt tasted sweeter to investors who paid 30 kobo more to take its stock to 38.80 naira. Ditto for National Salt Company which gained 15 kobo to close at 5.70 naira. West African Portland Cement was the sole gainer in the cement sector, adding 20 kobo to 37.65 naira. Benue Cement fell four kobo to 7.32 naira because of the large quantities on offer.
Oil shares were unusually quiet. Unipetrol, up 15 kobo at 46.15 naira and National Oil, 10 kobo stronger at 38.20 naira, advanced in the market's most active sector. Others were static. ($1=80 naira)
